introduction: At the advanced level, examiners test mathematical stability criteria like Routh-Hurwitz, the drawing rules of the Root Locus, and extracting Gain Margin (GM) and Phase Margin (PM) from Bode Plots.

core_concepts.title: Routh-Hurwitz Stability Criterion
core_concepts.description:
An algebraic method that determines how many poles of a system lie in the Right Half of the 's-plane' (RHP). 
**Condition:** If there is any sign change in the first column of the Routh array, the system is **Unstable**. The number of sign changes exactly equals the number of poles in the RHP.

core_concepts.title: Root Locus Technique
core_concepts.description:
A graphical representation of the path taken by closed-loop poles as the system gain ($K$) is varied from 0 to infinity ($\infty$). 
1. A root locus branch always starts from an open-loop pole ($K=0$) and terminates at an open-loop zero ($K=\infty$). 
2. The root locus is always entirely symmetrical about the real axis.

core_concepts.title: Bode Plot and Stability Margins
core_concepts.description:
A frequency domain analysis consisting of two plots: Magnitude (in dB) vs. $\log\omega$, and Phase angle vs. $\log\omega$.
- **Gain Margin (GM):** How much more gain can be added before the system becomes unstable.
- **Phase Margin (PM):** How much more phase lag can be added before the system becomes unstable.
**Stability Condition:** For a completely stable system, both GM and PM must be **Positive**.

important_entities.name: Nyquist Plot
important_entities.significance: Unlike Routh-Hurwitz, the Nyquist plot provides both absolute and relative stability metrics. The formula $N = Z - P$ ensures there are no closed-loop poles ($Z$) in the Right Half Plane to guarantee stability.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Advanced Exam Trap: What are the Gain Margin (GM) and Phase Margin (PM) for a system that is 'Marginally Stable' (oscillating continuously)? 
Remember, for a marginally stable system, **GM = 0 dB** and **PM = 0 degrees**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For a Stable system, the Phase Crossover Frequency ($\omega_{pc}$) is strictly greater than the Gain Crossover Frequency ($\omega_{gc}$). Therefore, $\omega_{pc} > \omega_{gc}$.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite ESE and GATE theoretical question: 'Where do the branches of a root locus terminate?' Answer: They terminate at open-loop Zeros or at Infinity.
